root.name: Grünfeld Defense: Stockholm Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Bg5

overview: White pins the knight with 4.Bg5 and Black usually responds 4...Ne4, when 5.Nxe4 dxe4 or 5.Bh4 Nxc3 6.bxc3 c5 give unbalanced pawn structures. White gets a strong centre and possible bishop pair, while Black has queenside counterplay and the long diagonal. Black has several equalising set-ups and strong players use it as a safe anti-Grünfeld.

white_ideas.idea: Build the centre with e3 and Nf3, using the bishop pair or space.
In the Taimanov line accept doubled c-pawns for an open b-file and active pieces.

black_ideas.idea: Strike the centre with ...c5 and ...Nc6 and use the g7 bishop.
Capture on c3 to give White doubled pawns and use the dark squares.

typical_structures.structure: White's doubled c-pawns against Black's ...c5 break in the Taimanov line; Grünfeld centre tension otherwise.

character.notes: Unbalanced pawn structures and piece play, but White's approach is a calmer sideline than the main Grünfeld.

structure.notes: Centre is in tension and pawns may be doubled; no locked centre.

approach.notes: A recognised anti-Grünfeld used by strong players.

level.notes: Needs structural judgement with doubled pawns more than raw memory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.Nxe4 dxe4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Bg5 Ne4 5. Nxe4 dxe4
sublines_that_differ.how: Simplifying line leading to a more positional game.

character.reason: Unbalanced structures but a calmer sideline than the main Grünfeld.

structure.reason: Centre in tension and pawn structure unsettled.

plans.reason: Doubled c-pawns for White and Black's attack on the centre.
